doubts.claim_under_doubt: verified means the manifest was verified clean by CI
doubts.summary: verified overclaimed execution-tier coverage (tests/coverage/acs), which are excluded from the structural comparator's exit code
doubts.resolution_note: corrected wording in module docstring + spec; cannot fix in code without violating the sub-iterate's own no-blocking-drift-check mandate

doubts.claim_under_doubt: no_record is a definite, completed negative answer
doubts.summary: the predicate's own commit regex accepted a 7-39 char abbreviation that GitHub's exact head_sha match turns into a false no_record

doubts.claim_under_doubt: the multi-run search cannot let a later rerun hide an earlier genuine pass
doubts.summary: jobs-endpoint per_page default (30) unhandled for an OS-matrixed run
doubts.resolution_note: added per_page=100 to the jobs-endpoint query

doubts.claim_under_doubt: pagination/rate-limiting cannot silently distort the outcome
doubts.summary: runs-list truncation silently downgraded to a false not_verified, total_count ignored
doubts.resolution_note: total_count vs fetched-page check added, returns error on detected truncation

doubts.claim_under_doubt: the three named compromise routes are exhaustive
doubts.summary: compromise-route enumeration omitted the gh/git binary and its environment, reachable on Windows via a plain working-tree write
doubts.resolution_note: amended the unforgeability sentence + Known Limitations bullet naming this as a repo-wide trust assumption; hardening it is out of this sub-iterate's scope

doubts.claim_under_doubt: an accepted run is a run of the ci.yml that already existed on main before the commit landed
doubts.summary: factually wrong about how GitHub Actions resolves a push-triggered workflow; also left ambiguous whether mandatory review is GitHub-enforced or Shipwright posture
doubts.resolution_note: rewrote the unforgeability paragraph in module docstring + spec to state the real mechanism and be explicit about posture vs enforcement

doubts.claim_under_doubt: AC9's multi-run search fully covers the rerun case
doubts.summary: the jobs query's default filter=latest means a manually re-run attempt can hide an earlier attempt's genuine confirmation
doubts.resolution_note: per-attempt querying is more surface than this predicate's size justifies for a scenario requiring a manual re-run of an already-successful run; Known Limitations bullet added

doubts.claim_under_doubt: all untrusted inputs to the API path are validated
doubts.summary: workflow_file unvalidated while commit was validated, despite both landing in the same request path

doubts.claim_under_doubt: renames are covered by the YAML-shape test
doubts.summary: a step-name or default-branch rename retroactively un-verifies every commit verified before the rename
doubts.resolution_note: Known Limitations bullet added; both are effectively append-only in practice

doubts.claim_under_doubt: prefer success if ANY job confirmed is the conservative reading
doubts.summary: under an OS matrix this is the permissive, not conservative, choice
doubts.resolution_note: documented the deliberate rationale in _provenance_step_conclusion's docstring

summary: 10 doubts: 2 high, 5 medium, 3 low. The API-side push/default-branch/conclusion trust filter itself could not be disproven — no PR-branch-only action produces a qualifying run object. 6 fixed in code, 4 disclosed with reasoning (each either explicitly out of this sub-iterate's mandate to fix, or disproportionate surface for the scenario it guards against).
